articles.summary: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PGE) today announced it has reached a major wildfire safety milestone, installing and energizing 1,500 miles of underground power lines in high fire-threat districts since launching its undergrounding program in 2021. Wildfire ignition risk on the 1,500 miles of undergrounded lines is permanently reduced by approximately 98%. Customers served by underground lines also experience approximately 90% fewer outages. "Undergrounding is one of the most powerful tools we have to protect our customers and communities from wildfire risk. Reaching 1,500 miles is an important milestone, but what matters most is what those miles deliver: safer communities, fewer outages, and more reliable electric service over decades for the customers we're privileged to serve. We're proud of this progress and remain focused on doing this work where it can deliver the greatest safety and reliability benefits," said Matt Pender, PGE Undergrounding and System Hardening
articles.title: PG&E Achieves 1,500-Mile Milestone in Major Wildfire Safety Undergrounding Effort

As communities celebrate National STEM Day on Nov. 8, the PGE Foundation reaffirms its commitment to building tomorrow's workforce through investments in STEM education and scholarships. This year, scholarships in the amounts of $2,500, $5,000 and $10,000 are being granted to 57 students from across Pacific Gas and Electric Company's (PGE) service area through the program. articles.summary: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PGE) is preparing for exceptionally high king tides this week that, combined with rain and wind, could create localized flooding and other weather-related impacts across Northern and Central California. PGE has activated its Emergency Operations Center and local and regional emergency centers to monitor conditions, assess potentially vulnerable infrastructure and position crews and equipment where they may be needed. The company is also coordinating with state and local emergency agencies as conditions develop. While king tides alone do not necessarily cause power outages, flooding, wind and other severe weather occurring at the same time can affect electric equipment or make it more difficult for crews to access damaged infrastructure. articles.title: Tides, Rain and Wind Across Northern and Central California

articles.summary: To help customers prepare their gas appliances for safe use during the cold weather months ahead, Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PGE) offers free in-home gas safety checks. During the gas safety checks, PGE also will re-light pilot lights for customers who have heaters or other appliances that have been turned off during warmer months. Free safety checks help ensure that gas appliances, including water heaters, furnaces and ovens, are operating safely and efficiently, reducing the risk of carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning within the home. Carbon monoxide is especially dangerous because it can't be seen, smelled or heard. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention , each year more than 400 Americans die from unintentional CO poisoning not linked to fires, more than 100,000 visit the emergency room, and more than 14,000 are hospitalized. articles.title: With Colder Weather Approaching, PG&E Offering Free Gas Appliance Safety Checks and Pilot Re-Lights

articles.summary: With the holidays upon us, Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PGE) urges customers not to allow utility scammers to take advantage of the hustle and bustle of the holiday season to steal your money through deceptive, high-pressure tactics. This Wednesday, November 18 is Utility Scam Awareness Day to drive awareness of the signs of a scam so that customers can avoid falling victim. Reports of scams targeting PGE customers have remained alarmingly high throughout 2026. In fact, there have been over 10,000 reports year-to-date with customer losses exceeding $300,000, and an average loss of $929. And, while scammers continuously adopt new methods to defraud utility customers, one common tactic is that they will demand that you make payment using a specific method, such as visiting a payment kiosk at a store, or by pre-paid debit cards or money transfer services to avoid immediate disconnection of your utility services. articles.title: PG&E Warns Customers to "Skip the Kiosk" to Avoid Utility Scams
